title: wewf-world-championship
label: Volcano

won.source: The report's own words: Volcano "defeated the former champ Joe 'Brick' Wall."

how: Beat Joe "Brick" Wall for the vacated-by-loss title, defended it against Irving Forbush, "Irish" Mike Flint and Mr. Roddy, then lost it the same turn.
note: Predecessor reign (Joe "Brick" Wall's own) is not attested in the held record beyond the report's own "the former champ" phrase — a gap, not a claim of a vacant title.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: Juggernaut

won.source: The report's own words: Juggernaut "barely pinned Volcano" to become "the 8th WeWF World Champion."

how: Barely pinned Volcano.
note: Held the belt for almost a month, through the unheld Report #7 and a five-defense week in Report #8, before the General beat him by five points in Report #9. The reign's own end is now dated from the wing's own weekly record.

title: wewf-americas-championship
label: The Feral Frog

won.source: The report's own intro: "The Leaping Lords were also successful this turn, taking two Continental Titles."

how: Took the Americas Championship in turn 6, per the report's own intro; the specific title-deciding bout within the Continental Titles match block is not disambiguated by the report's own text.
note: Photon Torpedo is the Americas Champion in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991, and Admiral Chekov's own line in Report #9 dates the change — “Photon Torpedo DID become the first wrestler in WeWF history to win a Continental title while ranked DEAD LAST in the ratings!” The change itself falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

title: wewf-eurasia-championship
label: The Lethal Lemming

won.source: The report's own intro: "The Leaping Lords were also successful this turn, taking two Continental Titles."

how: Took the Eurasia Championship in turn 6, per the report's own intro; the specific title-deciding bout within the Continental Titles match block is not disambiguated by the report's own text.
note: “Irish” Mike Flint is the Eurasia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991. The change falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: The Crusher

won.source: The report's own intro: "The Crusher, managed by their arch-enemy Simon Bolendorf, took the Africa/Australia Belt."

how: Took the Africa/Australia Championship in turn 6, per the report's own intro; the specific title-deciding bout within the Continental Titles match block is not disambiguated by the report's own text.
note: The General is the Africa/Australia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991, where the report also credits him with a successful defense. The change falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Dynamic Machine

won.source: The report's own headline: "The Dynamic Machine Regains Tag-Team Belts!"

how: Regained the Tag Team Championship in turn 6 with 145 points — the league's points-based tag standings, not a single decisive title bout.
note: The Leaping Lords are the Tag Team Champions in Report #8's own ranking table of 17 February 1991, and its own headline calls that reign a regain. The change falls inside the unheld Report #7; a gap, not a claim.

title: wewf-twiw-tv-championship
label: Mr. B

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. B is the TWIW TV Champion on the newsdesk's own broadcast of 30 January 1992, and the broadcast of 15 February says he had held it “for the better part of a month.” The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to the Hangman on a flying powerslam off the top turnbuckle, after being hung over the top rope with the Hangman’s own noose while the referee was down.
note: On 30 January he kept the belt on a disqualification he was himself the subject of, when the guest announcer left the booth to attack the challenger.

title: wewf-twiw-tv-tag-team-championship
label: The Annihilation Alliance

won.source: Now dated from the tournament's own final, 31 March 1992: “A quick pin, and we have the first TWIW tag team champions!”

how: Won the four-round, eight-team TWIW TV Tag Team Title Tournament, beating the WeWF's own tag champions Flint and Steel in the final; retained against Carnage in a steel cage rematch on 13 April.
note: Still champions at the held record's end. THE REIGN'S OWN START WAS UNRECOVERED AND IS NOW DATED to the tournament final that the 13 April broadcast calls “a rematch of what I call the finals.”

title: wewf-world-championship
label: The General

won.source: Report #9's own headline: “The General beat Juggernaut to become the 10th WeWF World Champion!”

how: Beat Juggernaut by five points after Photon Torpedo had beaten him by disqualification and “Irish” Mike Flint had taken him to three.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: Frank Steel

won.source: Report #11's own headline: “The Americas Champion, Frank Steel beat the General to win the WeWF World Title!”

how: Beat the General while holding the Americas Championship, and won the Tag Team Championship with his own partner in the same turn — three belts at once, which is why the Americas Championship was declared vacant.
note: The report calls it his second reign; the first is not attested in the held record.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: The General (second reign)

won.source: Report #18's own headline: “The General beat Frank Steel to regain the WeWF World Championship!”

how: Beat an exhausted Frank Steel, who had won only two of his five title matches that week.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: DiMadMan

won.source: Report #19's own headline: “DiMadMan Wins World Title!”

how: Beat the General, and vacated his own Africa/Australia Championship on winning it.
note: Still champion in Report #20 (12 May 1991); the General is champion again at the start of Report #22’s own week. The change falls inside the unheld Report #21. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: The General (third reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: the General is the reigning champion at the start of Report #22's own week (26 May 1991), having regained the belt inside the unheld Report #21. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to the Big Kahuna in the first of three title changes inside one week.
note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: The Big Kahuna

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “The Big Kahuna defeated the General to win the title, but then lost it to Bjorn ‘the Sweedish Pretzel’.”

how: Beat the General, then lost to Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” the same week.
note: One of three World Championship changes inside a single week — the only such week in the surviving record.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”

won.source: Report #22's own headline.

how: Beat the Big Kahuna, then lost to “Irish” Mike Flint the same week.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: “Irish” Mike Flint

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “‘Irish’ Mike Flint then beat Bjorn to win the WeWF World Championship! This is the second time he has held the belt.”

how: Beat Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”, and carried the belt into the Summer League as its own standing champion.
note: The report calls it his second reign; the first is not attested in the held record.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: The Big Kahuna (second reign)

won.source: Summer Report #4's own call: “The Big Kahuna wins the World Championship back from the man who took it from him right before the Summer League started!”

how: Beat “Irish” Mike Flint on a big splash, in Flint’s second title match of the same night.
note: Still champion in Summer Report #5 (28 July 1991); Mr. Roddy is champion by Summer Report #9 (25 August). The change falls inside the unheld Summer Reports #6–#8. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: Mr. Roddy

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. Roddy is the reigning champion in Summer Report #9's own standings (25 August 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to the General on a bulldog off the top rope.
note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: The General (fourth reign)

won.source: Report #32's own call: “The General regains the WeWF World Title for an unprecedented fourth time!”

how: Beat Mr. Roddy on a bulldog off the top rope — the first man to hold the belt four times, ahead of Volcano and “Irish” Mike Flint on three.
note: Steelgrave is champion by Report #37 (28 October 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #33–#36. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: Steelgrave

won.source: Not directly attested: Steelgrave is the reigning champion in Report #37's own standings (28 October 1991), and defends the belt in Reports #37 and #38. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Defended against the Sandman (by disqualification) and the Millionaire (a power bomb) in the two held reports of his own reign.
note: Mr. Roddy is champion again by the newsdesk’s own standings of 30 January 1992. The change falls inside the unheld Reports #39–#49. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: Mr. Roddy (second reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. Roddy is the reigning champion in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 30 January 1992. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

note: The Sandman is champion by the newsdesk’s own standings of 15 February 1992. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: The Sandman

won.source: Not directly attested: the Sandman is the reigning champion in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 15 February 1992, and Report #50 says he “held that belt for almost a month.” The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to Metal on a powerslam, with nobody in his corner.
note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-world-championship
label: Metal

won.source: Report #50's own call: “Metal defeats The Sandman to win the WeWF World Title!”

how: Picked the Sandman up over his shoulder and powerslammed him.
note: Still champion at the held record's end; no later WeWF report survives.

title: wewf-americas-championship
label: Photon Torpedo

won.source: Not directly attested: Photon Torpedo is the Americas Champion in Report #8's own ranking table (17 February 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to Frank Steel.
note: Won inside the unheld Report #7. Admiral Chekov’s own line in Report #9 dates it: “Photon Torpedo DID become the first wrestler in WeWF history to win a Continental title while ranked DEAD LAST in the ratings!”

title: wewf-americas-championship
label: Frank Steel

won.source: Report #9's own ranking table: “Americas Champion: Frank Steel.”

how: Vacated: on winning the World Championship he held three belts at once, and the report declared the Americas Championship vacant with a tournament to fill it.

title: wewf-americas-championship
label: FireLord

won.source: Report #12's own headline: “FireLord wins Americas' Title!”

how: Won the eight-man tournament for the vacant belt — Incision in the first round, Mr. Roddy in the second, Juggernaut in the final.
note: The Re-Animator is champion by Report #15 (7 April 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #13 and #14. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-americas-championship
label: The Re-Animator

won.source: Not directly attested: the Re-Animator is the Americas Champion in Report #15's own ranking table (7 April 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to the Big Kahuna in his second defense of that week.
note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-americas-championship
label: The Big Kahuna

won.source: Report #20's own headline: “The Big Kahuna Wins Americas' Title!”

how: Lost to the Re-Animator in a no-disqualification, no-time-limit main event, submitting to a Boston crab.

title: wewf-americas-championship
label: The Re-Animator (second reign)

won.source: Supercard #4's own ring announcement: “Here is your winner, and NEW Americas' Champion, the Re-Animator!”

how: Submitted the Big Kahuna to a Boston crab in the Supercard main event.
note: The championship does not appear again: the Summer League that began a fortnight later ran a World, a United States and a Tag Team Championship only. Whether it was retired or simply not defended is not stated anywhere in the surviving record.

title: wewf-eurasia-championship
label: “Irish” Mike Flint

won.source: Not directly attested: “Irish” Mike Flint is the Eurasia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table (17 February 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to Destruction.
note: Won inside the unheld Report #7. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-eurasia-championship
label: Destruction

won.source: Report #9's own ranking table: “Eurasia Champion: Destruction.”

how: Lost to AquaDemon.

title: wewf-eurasia-championship
label: AquaDemon

won.source: Report #12's own headline: “FireLord's partner, AquaDemon, won the Eurasia Title.”

how: Beat Destruction, one of two Elementals to take a Continental belt in the same turn.
note: “Irish” Mike Flint is champion again by Report #15 (7 April 1991). A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-eurasia-championship
label: “Irish” Mike Flint (second reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: “Irish” Mike Flint is the Eurasia Champion in Report #15's own ranking table (7 April 1991) and holds it through Report #20 (12 May 1991). The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

note: BudMan is champion by the week of Report #22, which has the Millionaire taking the belt from him. The change falls inside the unheld Report #21. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-eurasia-championship
label: BudMan

won.source: Not directly attested: Report #22 records the Millionaire winning the Eurasia Title “from BudMan”, which is the whole of the evidence for BudMan’s own reign. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to the Millionaire.
note: Won and lost inside eight days, one end of it in an unheld report. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-eurasia-championship
label: The Millionaire

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “the Millionaire won the Eurasia Title from BudMan!”

how: Beat BudMan.
note: The championship does not appear again: the Summer League that began a fortnight later ran three belts only.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: The General

won.source: Not directly attested: the General is the Africa/Australia Champion in Report #8's own ranking table (17 February 1991), where the report also credits him with a successful defense. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost the belt to Mr. Roddy in the same turn in which he won the World Championship.
note: Won inside the unheld Report #7. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: Mr. Roddy

won.source: Report #9's own headline: “The General lost his Africa/Australia belt to Mr. Roddy.”

how: Lost to Tom “the Animal” Brown after outside interference by the Mexican Bandit.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: Tom “the Animal” Brown

won.source: Report #11's own headline: “Tom ‘the Animal’ Brown takes Africa/Australia Belt!”

how: Lost to DiMadMan.
note: The report credits the win to “outside interference by the Mexican Bandit”, and its own comments have Mr. Roddy working out that the Bandit’s initials are Mr. B’s.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: DiMadMan

won.source: Report #12's own ranking table: “Africa/Australia Champion: DiMadMan (9-0-1).”

how: Beat Tom “the Animal” Brown.
note: WindWarrior is champion by Report #15 (7 April 1991). A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: WindWarrior

won.source: Not directly attested: Report #15's own headline has him taking it — “One of their members, WindWarrior, took the Africa/Australia Championship this week” — in the same issue whose ranking table first carries him. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to DiMadMan.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: DiMadMan (second reign)

won.source: Report #16's own headline: “DiMadMan, after losing the Tag Team belts, came back to regain the Africa/Australia Championship!”

how: Vacated on winning the World Championship; a tournament was announced to fill it.

title: wewf-africa-australia-championship
label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”

won.source: Report #20's own headline: “Bjorn ‘the Sweedish Pretzel’ Wins Tournament!”

how: Won the tournament for the vacant belt across three nights inside one turn — Virus on the Wednesday, Mr. Roddy on the Thursday, Frank Steel in Friday’s final.
note: The championship does not appear again: the Summer League that began a fortnight later ran three belts only.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Leaping Lords

won.source: Not directly attested: the Leaping Lords are the Tag Team Champions in Report #8's own ranking table, and its own headline calls the reign a regain — “The Leaping Lords Regain Tag Belts!” The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to the Maniacs at the league’s own first Supercard.
note: A regain, so an intervening reign exists that this collection does not hold. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Maniacs

won.source: Report #10's own headline: “The Maniacs beat the Leaping Lords at the Supercard, and then successfully defended the belts this week!”

how: Lost to Flint and Steel in a very close match.
note: Won at the league’s own first Supercard, held on Thursday 28 February 1991; the Supercard itself does not survive.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: Flint and Steel

won.source: Report #11's own headline: “Flint and Steel Take Tag Titles!”

how: Beat the Maniacs, then made two more defenses the same turn.
note: The Intoxicators are champions by Report #15 (7 April 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #13 and #14. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Intoxicators

won.source: Not directly attested: Report #15's own headline has them taking it — “Intoxicators Take Tag Belts! DiMadMan and BudMan beat RnR after the Highlanders had beaten RnR by DQ”. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to Flint and Steel.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: Flint and Steel (second held reign)

won.source: Report #16's own headline: “Flint and Steel defeated the Intoxicators to win the Tag Team Titles for the third time!”

how: Lost to the Law in the Law’s own first defense as a full-time team.
note: The report calls it their third reign; this collection holds the second and the third but not the first.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Law

won.source: Report #19's own headline: “The Law Takes Tag Titles!”

how: Lost to the Highlanders.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Highlanders

won.source: Report #20's own headline: “Highlanders Take Tag Belts!”

how: Lost the belts back to the Law.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Law (second reign)

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “the Law regained the Tag Team Titles from the Highlanders”.

how: Lost to the Hoosiers in the Hoosiers’ own seventh match as a team.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Hoosiers

won.source: Summer Report #2's own call: “The Hoosiers win the match! We have new champions!”

how: Lost to Flint and Steel after more than twenty minutes.
note: The Four Corners laid the new champions and their manager out with the belts themselves minutes after the title change — the ambush that starts the summer’s central feud.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: Flint and Steel (third held reign)

won.source: Summer Report #4's own call: “Flint and Steel win the tag team titles!”

how: Lost to RnR in the August Supercard main event.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: RnR

won.source: The August Supercard's own call: “RnR are the new WeWF Tag Team Champions!”

how: Won when both legal men were unconscious and the Millionaire happened to be lying on top of Frank Steel.
note: The Klingons are champions by Report #37 (28 October 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Reports #33–#36. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Klingons

won.source: Not directly attested: the Klingons are the Tag Team Champions in Report #37's own standings (28 October 1991), and defend the belts in Reports #37 and #38. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Defended against the Maniacs on the Klinshai Bombing, and kept the belts by disqualification against the Hoosiers when their own manager shook the ropes.
note: The Hoosiers are champions by the newsdesk’s own standings of 30 January 1992. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Hoosiers (second reign)

won.source: Not directly attested: the Hoosiers are the Tag Team Champions in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 30 January 1992. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to the Law.
note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-tag-team-championship
label: The Law (third reign)

won.source: The newsdesk's own call, 15 February 1992: “The winners, and for the third time WeWF Tag Team Champions: The Law!” — a count this ledger's own three reigns for them match exactly.

how: Judge Dredd cradled Erik while Machiavelli distracted the referee and Judge Anderson shook the top rope to drop Daemon off it.
note: Still champions at the held record's end, having defended against the Hoosiers and the Cochon Brothers.

title: wewf-united-states-championship
label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel”

won.source: Summer Report #1's own call: “Your winner, and new US Champion, Bjorn ‘the Sweedish Pretzel’!”

how: Won the sixteen-man tournament that created the championship, beating BudMan in the final on his own leglock.
note: Mr. B is champion by Summer Report #9 (25 August 1991). The change falls inside the unheld Summer Reports #6–#8. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-united-states-championship
label: Mr. B

won.source: Not directly attested: Mr. B is the United States Champion in Summer Report #9's own standings (25 August 1991), and defends the belt there and at the August Supercard. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Lost to Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” on a sleeper, with Victor Rivera Jr. pulling the ropes out of reach.
note: A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-united-states-championship
label: Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” (second reign)

won.source: Report #32's own call: “Bjorn ‘The Swedish Pretzel’ regains the US Title!”

how: Lost to the General, who wrestled with his head bandaged from an ambush an hour earlier.

title: wewf-united-states-championship
label: The General

won.source: Report #37's own ring call: “Here is your winner, and NEW US CHAMPION, The General!”

how: Beat Bjorn “the Sweedish Pretzel” on a brainbuster after rolling away from a fistdrop off the top rope.
note: Black Tiger is champion by the newsdesk’s own standings of 30 January 1992, undefeated at 6-0. A gap, not a claim: the reports that would carry the change do not survive.

title: wewf-united-states-championship
label: Black Tiger

won.source: Not directly attested: Black Tiger is the United States Champion in the newsdesk's own WeWF standings of 30 January 1992, at 6-0. The date recorded is the date of that document; precision circa, meaning won on or before it.

how: Defended against “Gentleman” Jim Gilette on a backslide and against Zangief the Terrible on a cradle suplex, and challenged the whole federation to a caged battle royal for the belt.
note: Still champion at the held record's end, and still unbeaten.

title: wewf-six-man-championship
label: Apocalypse Now

won.source: Report #15's own headline: “Apocalypse Now Take Six Man Belts! The three masked men calling themselves Apocalypse Now beat the Superstars to take the Six Man Titles.”

how: Lost to the Down-Under Decking Crew.
note: The championship appears for the first time in the same report that records this reign; whether it existed before is not stated.

title: wewf-six-man-championship
label: The Down-Under Decking Crew

won.source: Report #22's own headline: “The Down-Under Decking Crew beat Apocalypse Now for the Six-Man Titles.”

how: Beat Apocalypse Now.
note: The last word on the belts is the newsdesk’s own, in Report #38 of 10 November 1991: “Devastation, Inc. still have the WeWF 6-man belts … even though those titles have been retired,” and “they only hold two-thirds. No way would Mr. B give them his third of the title.” The championship was retired with its holders split up.

title: wewf-twiw-tv-championship
label: Hangman

won.source: Now dated from the newsdesk's own broadcast of 15 February 1992: the Hangman hung Mr. B over the top rope with his own noose while the referee was down, then hit a flying powerslam off the top turnbuckle for the three.

how: Beat Mr. B on the newsdesk's own broadcast of 15 February 1992, and retained against Mr. B again, against Lancelot by countout, against Freddie “Fair Play” Fitness and against Uncle Nasty.
note: Still champion at the held record's end. THE REIGN'S OWN START WAS UNRECOVERED AND IS NOW DATED from the newsdesk's own broadcast of 15 February 1992; the reigns on this belt were renumbered into date order in the same pass.

title: wewf-battle-royal
label: RnR

won.source: the wing's own Supercard #4 of 29 May 1991, which introduces Mr. Roddy as “one half of the winning team in the Tag Team Battle Royal” (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-supercard-4-1991-05-29.html)

how: Won the sixteen-team Tag Team Battle Royal, and were attacked by the Four Corners the moment the match ended — the run-in that turned the 007 Special against them.

title: wewf-battle-royal
label: The Unknown Masked Wrestler

won.source: the wing's own Report #9 of 24 February 1991 (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-report-9-1991-02-24.html)

how: Won the league's first battle royal and took $100,000 from Mr. Fujikuchi's Akira Foundation; refused to give the interviewer his name, and shoved her when she reached for the mask.

title: wewf-battle-royal
label: Bjorn "The Sweedish Pretzel"

won.source: the wing's own Report #17 of 21 April 1991 (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-report-17-1991-04-21.html)

how: Won the Team Challenge Series battle royal, eliminating both of Flint and Steel at the end — “although he had some help.”

title: wewf-iron-man-trophy
label: The Big Kahuna

won.source: the wing's own Supercard 5 of 31 July 1991, whose commentary calls him the winner of the previous Supercard's Iron Man Tournament (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-supercard-5-1991-07-31.html)

how: Won the first Iron Man Tournament, at the Supercard of 30 April 1991, beating the Romulan Mauler in the final round.
note: Retained the trophy in a four-man round robin against the Executioner, the Plaid Powerhouse and Photon Torpedo, finishing unbeaten at 3-0; he carried the cup onto Malibu's Bikini Shop a fortnight later. Source: the wing's own August Supercard (promotions/wewf/archive/wewf-august-supercard-1991-08-31.html).
